tour.overview:
Lake Eyasi, a seasonal soda lake south-west of the Ngorongoro Highlands, is home to the Hadzabe, one of the last peoples in Africa who live largely as hunter-gatherers, speaking a language with click sounds unrelated to any other. Nearby live the Datoga, pastoralists known for their skills as blacksmiths. Visits to these communities must be made with care and respect.

This private day takes you there with a licensed guide and a local interpreter, in a way that respects the communities and ensures fees are paid directly to them.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours from Karatu
• Start and end: your hotel in Karatu or Arusha
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver; local interpreter
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; walking in the bush

WHAT YOU SEE
• A Hadzabe camp.
• A Datoga homestead.
• Lake Eyasi.

WHY THIS WORKS
Your guide and interpreter make the visit a genuine exchange rather than a show, at a pace set by the community.

WHO IT SUITS
Culturally curious travellers and photographers who ask before taking pictures.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For wildlife, choose our Ngorongoro or Tarangire day safaris.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The day starts very early to join the Hadzabe in the morning. Always ask before photographing anyone. Participation in a hunt is not guaranteed and is entirely the community’s choice.

days.name: A morning with the Hadzabe, Datoga blacksmiths and Lake Eyasi
days.description:
What to expect: two communities of the Eyasi basin and the lake, with a guide, interpreter, community fees and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you before dawn in Karatu and drive down to the Eyasi basin. With your interpreter, you join a Hadzabe group at their camp, where they may share how they make fire with sticks, prepare bows and arrows, and gather roots, berries and honey. If the group goes out to forage or hunt, you may walk with them at a respectful distance, as they read tracks and the calls of the honeyguide bird. Your guide explains the challenges they face as their land shrinks.

You then visit a Datoga family, whose blacksmiths melt scrap metal to forge arrowheads, which they trade with the Hadzabe, and bracelets. After lunch near the lake, with its views of the escarpment and onion fields, you return to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
05:30 – Pick-up in Karatu.
07:00 – Morning with the Hadzabe.
10:30 – Datoga blacksmiths.
12:00 – Lake Eyasi viewpoint.
12:30 – Lunch.
14:30 – Back in Karatu.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Ask before taking photos and follow your guide’s advice.
• Bring closed shoes for walking in the bush.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, interpreter, community fees, lunch, bottled water.
NOT INCLUDED: purchases, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is this visit ethical?
faq.answer: We work with local guides and pay fees directly to the communities; visits are small and respectful.

faq.question: Will we go hunting?
faq.answer: Only if the community chooses to go out; it is never staged.

faq.question: Can we take photos?
faq.answer: Ask first, through your interpreter; some people may decline.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for curious children who can be respectful and walk in the bush.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly; walking in the bush is on uneven ground.

faq.question: Why such an early start?
faq.answer: The Hadzabe are most active in the cool early morning.

faq.question: Can we combine it with Ngorongoro?
What should we wear?
faq.answer: Neutral clothes, closed shoes, a hat and sun protection.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: June to October, the dry season.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary on safari in Tanzania: guides, drivers and camp staff appreciate a tip if you were happy with their service, but it is always your choice. Your guide can suggest typical amounts.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
